title: Projective cofibrancy under enlargement of a finite-pattern universe
statement:
Fix nested Grothendieck universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $P=(B,S,\{K_a^{\triangleleft}\to B\})$ be a $\mathcal U$-small categorical pattern of [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], with all $2$-simplices scaled and every $K_a$ having finitely many nondegenerate simplices (the empty shape is allowed). Write $\mathsf M_{P,\mathcal W}$ for the marked pattern model category of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] in universe $\mathcal W$, and $\iota$ for inclusion of the smaller marked simplicial objects into the larger ones. Use the common generators, weak equivalences and fibrant replacements of [lem-coef-finite-pattern-universe-comparison].

Let $I$ be a $\mathcal U$-small fibrant simplicial category: it has a small set of objects, small simplicial mapping sets that are Kan complexes, and associative unital simplicial composition. Give the enriched functor categories $\mathsf M_{P,\mathcal W}^I$ the projective model structures of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams]. The inclusion $\iota^I$ sends every projective cofibration between $\mathcal U$-small enriched diagrams to a projective cofibration in the larger diagram category. In particular, if $QF\to F$ is a projectively cofibrant replacement in the smaller category, then the same arrow is a projectively cofibrant replacement in the larger category. It also sends every projectively cofibrant-fibrant diagram to a projectively cofibrant-fibrant diagram. Here a projectively cofibrant replacement is an objectwise trivial fibration with projectively cofibrant source; projective fibrations and weak equivalences are objectwise.

source.place: Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remarks A.3.3.4-A.3.3.5, printed pp.869-870 (PDF pp.887-888): projective enriched structures and free-diagram cells. The universe-enlargement consequence is agent-written from this cellular description and the common finite-pattern generators, not a separately numbered theorem. No Stacks tag states this enriched model-category result.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus] in both universes: these are combinatorial simplicial model categories. The small fibrant simplicial category $I$ is eligible for the projective structures and free-generator assertion of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams]. To supply its rectification parameters if needed, take $K=N_{\mathrm{hc}}I$ and the counit $\mathfrak C[K]\to I$. By [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], this is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence: the Quillen equivalence criterion applies to the cofibrant simplicial set $N_{\mathrm{hc}}I$ and fibrant $I$, and the adjoint of this counit is the identity. The sets of simplicial functors defining $K_n$ are small, so $K$ is small in the same universe. Write $G$ for the common set of marked cofibration generators supplied by [lem-coef-finite-pattern-universe-comparison]. In either universe every projective cofibration is a retract of a relative cell map generated by $F_i(g)$, where $i\in\operatorname{Ob}I$, $g\in G$ and $F_i(A)(j)=I(i,j)\otimes A$.

source.place: Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remark A.3.3.5, printed pp.870-871; free-diagram generating cofibrations. Coherent-nerve Quillen equivalence supplies optional rectification parameters.

proof.text: The free diagrams in step 1 are the same after inclusion. Indeed the simplicial tensor by a simplicial set $L$ is $A\times L^\sharp$: its maps into $Z$ are the maps $L\to\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_B(A,Z)$ by the mapping formula of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus]. Its degree $n$ is $A_n\times L_n$, its marked edges are the pairs with marked $A$-coordinate, and its base map is projection through $A$. These products, markings, and the action induced by the composition of $I$ are identical in the two universes. Since every $I(i,j)$ and every endpoint of $g\in G$ is small, so is $F_i(g)$, by closure of the smaller universe under products and small families. Thus inclusion identifies the free generators themselves, not just their evaluations up to weak equivalence.

source.place: Remark A.3.3.5, free diagram formula; degreewise expansion for marked pattern objects.

proof.text: Inclusion preserves the small colimits used in cell attachments. For a small diagram of marked objects over $(B,S)$, take in each degree the disjoint union of its sets modulo the relations imposed by its arrows, with the induced map to $B$. Mark exactly the images of marked edges. Faces and degeneracies descend, and maps out of this quotient are precisely compatible families of marked maps over $B$. The same quotient computes the colimit in either universe and stays small. For a diagram of enriched $I$-diagrams perform this construction at every object $j$. The action of $I(j,k)_n$ sends the class of $x\in D_t(j)_n$ to the class of its action on $x$ in $D_t(k)_n$. Naturality of the transition maps makes this independent of the representative; the simplicial identities, units and associativity descend from each $D_t$. The quotient universal property also gives the enriched naturality of the induced maps. Hence these are colimits in the enriched functor category in both universes. This includes initial diagrams, coproducts, pushouts and ordinal colimits indexed in the smaller universe.

source.place: Agent-written degreewise colimit verification for the marked slice and its enriched diagrams, supporting the cellular argument of Remark A.3.3.5.

proof.text: Let $h$ be any projective cofibration between smaller diagrams. Use its retract-of-cells presentation from step 1 in the smaller model category. All coproduct index sets, its ordinal, all intermediate diagrams and all its structure maps belong to the smaller universe; in particular the same ordinal is allowed in the larger universe. Step 2 identifies every attached free generator, and step 3 preserves every attaching pushout, coproduct and limit-stage colimit. The resulting larger relative cell map therefore has the included $h$ as an arrow retract: the two retract squares and their identity equation are preserved by the inclusion functor. This retract is a projective cofibration in the larger structure. Indeed, by the enriched Yoneda lemma and the tensor adjunction, maps $F_i(A)\to D$ correspond to maps $A\to D(i)$, so a lifting problem of $F_i(g)$ against a map $D\to D'$ is a lifting problem of $g$ against its component at $i$. A projective trivial fibration is an objectwise trivial fibration, since projective fibrations and weak equivalences are objectwise, and $g$ is a cofibration; so each $F_i(g)$ lifts against all projective trivial fibrations and is a projective cofibration. The left class of the projective model weak factorization system is closed under coproducts, pushouts, transfinite composites and retracts. Applying this to the initial map, whose initial diagram is preserved by step 3, proves preservation of projectively cofibrant objects.

source.place: Remark A.3.3.5, applied to the same relative free-cell presentation in the two universes.

proof.text: Let $p:X\to Y$ be a trivial fibration between smaller pattern objects. In the smaller model structure it lifts against every cofibration, hence every $g:D\to E$ in the common set $G$. A square from this same $g$ to the included $p$ in the larger category consists only of maps between smaller marked simplicial sets over $B$. These maps and their equations are the very same functions in the smaller category, so the smaller lift is also a larger lift. Thus the included $p$ has the right lifting property against every element of $G$.

source.place: Agent-written lifting-square comparison using the common generators; model weak factorization systems as defined in lem-coef-simplicial-model-coherent-diagrams.

proof.text: This lifting property implies that the included $p$ is a trivial fibration in the larger pattern model. To see the implication explicitly, lifts against a coproduct of $G$ are chosen summand by summand. A pushout square has the same lifting problem by its universal property. Along a relative $G$-cell map choose these lifts successively, extending the lift already chosen; at a limit ordinal use their compatible colimit map. This transfinite recursion is in the larger universe, so it also treats larger cell presentations. An arrow retract inherits a lift by composing its section, the cell-map lift, and its retraction. By [lem-coef-finite-pattern-universe-comparison] every larger cofibration is such a retract. Therefore the included $p$ lifts against every larger cofibration, and the model weak factorization system makes it a trivial fibration. No assertion that an arbitrary larger lifting problem is a smaller one was used.

source.place: Agent-written coproduct, pushout, transfinite and retract lifting argument; model weak factorization systems and the common cofibration-cell description.

proof.text: Now let $QF\to F$ be the given smaller projectively cofibrant replacement. Its component at every object of $I$ is a trivial fibration, since projective fibrations and weak equivalences are objectwise. Steps 5-6 preserve each component as a trivial fibration in the larger pattern model. Consequently the same diagram arrow is a projective trivial fibration in the larger diagram model. Its source is projectively cofibrant by step 4, giving exactly the required replacement, with the same arrow and source; it is not necessary to identify independently chosen replacement functors.

source.place: Proposition A.3.3.2 and Definition A.3.3.1, objectwise projective fibrations and weak equivalences.

proof.text: Finally, a smaller projectively fibrant diagram has fibrant values, since its map to the terminal diagram is objectwise a fibration. Every value remains fibrant by [lem-coef-finite-pattern-universe-comparison], whose finite-cone hypotheses are precisely those assumed for $P$ here. Hence its inclusion is again projectively fibrant. Together with step 4 this preserves projectively cofibrant-fibrant diagrams. The argument also covers empty $I$, empty cone shapes and empty generating index sets: the colimits, products and lifting tests retain their empty-family meanings.

source.place: Proposition A.3.3.2; objectwise projective fibrancy combined with the finite-pattern universe comparison.

proof_origin.place: Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remark A.3.3.5 read online, printed pp.870-871 (PDF pp.887-888); agent-written universe comparison by degreewise colimits and lifting. HTT is not archived under literature/.
